questions.question:
D3 — Bind `userId` as a query parameter, or keep the raw SQL fragment?
Project/branch/task: Payment Processing Integration plan on `main`, HOLD SCOPE review, ledger row D3.
ELI10: The user ID arrives from Stripe's event metadata. The signature proves Stripe sent it; it does not prove the string is harmless. Anyone who can set PaymentIntent metadata on your Stripe account (a merchant tool, a leaked API key) can put `'; DROP TABLE users; --` in it, and the plan's own contracts say IDs may contain any punctuation and nothing sanitizes them. Pasting that string into SQL text is classic SQL injection; handing it to the database as a bound parameter makes it inert.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Data exfiltration or destruction through a validly signed webhook, with no alert distinguishing it from a normal payment.
Recommendation: A because binding costs one line and removes the whole vulnerability class; the plan's own contracts section already states a valid signature does not make the string safe for SQL.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=2/10
Net: a one-line binding versus an injection hole reachable by anyone with metadata access.

options.label: Bound parameter / finder (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Quotes, semicolons, Unicode in `metadata.user_id` become plain data, never SQL
✅ Uses the shared DB client the way it is designed; no format validation added, opaque TEXT contract intact
❌ Requires one deliberate line instead of string interpolation

options.label: Keep raw SQL fragment
options.description:
✅ Matches the plan text as written; nothing to change
✅ Marginally shorter code
❌ SQL injection through any validly signed event whose metadata an attacker controls

questions.question:
D1 — How deep should the successful-charge test assert?
Project/branch/task: main, HOLD SCOPE review of the processPayment test-coverage plan (ledger row D1).
ELI10: The plan says the receipt must be exactly { chargeId: "ch_paid", amountCents: 1000, currency: "USD" }, but the planned test only checks that *something* came back. A receipt of {} or one with the wrong amount would still pass. The factory already exposes the Stripe call history and the sleeper record, so stronger assertions cost lines, not infrastructure.
Stakes if we pick wrong: a regression that drops currency or mis-copies the amount ships with a green suite, and the customer sees a wrong receipt.
Recommendation: C because the plan's own stated goal is coverage of this contract, and C is three assertions using hooks the plan already names (human: ~10 min / CC: ~1 min).
Completeness: A=3/10, B=7/10, C=10/10
Net: trading two extra assertion lines against a test that can actually fail when the receipt contract breaks.

options.label: C) Full: receipt + call + no backoff (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Deep-equal the receipt AND assert exactly one Stripe charge call with amount 1000 / USD AND an empty sleeper record. Covers the whole happy-path contract.
❌ Three assertions instead of one; pins a 'no backoff on success' fact the plan implies but does not spell out.

options.label: B) Deep-equal receipt only
options.description:
✅ One assertion covers all three receipt fields; a dropped or mis-copied field fails the test.
❌ Says nothing about what was sent to Stripe or whether a backoff fired on the happy path.

options.label: A) Keep as planned: truthy only
options.description:
✅ Matches PLAN.md verbatim; smallest possible diff.
❌ Passes when the receipt is {} or carries the wrong amount; does not cover the contract the plan claims to cover.

answers.D1 — How deep should the successful-char: C) Full: receipt + call + no backoff (recommended)

questions.question:
D2 — How should the new lookup put request.params.userId into the query?
Project/branch/task: main — Payment Processing Integration, HOLD SCOPE review, ledger row D2.
ELI10: The user ID arrives from Stripe metadata as any text at all, including quotes, semicolons and Unicode, and nothing upstream cleans it (PLAN.md:21-26). The plan pastes that text straight into a SQL string. A real user whose ID contains an apostrophe breaks the query every time, so their payment is never marked paid and Stripe keeps retrying for three days. If anyone can influence a stored user ID, the same paste becomes SQL injection with a valid Stripe signature on it.
Stakes if we pick wrong: stuck payments for legitimate IDs plus an injection surface on the payments path; both retryable forever, neither self-healing.
Recommendation: A because a bound parameter keeps the "every nonempty string is a valid identifier" invariant by construction and has no charset edge cases.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=6/10, C=2/10
Pros / cons:
A) Bound parameter or existing ORM finder (recommended)
  ✅ Injection impossible by construction; no charset or escape-mode edge cases to audit
  ✅ Same semantics as the existing lookup the plan says it retains (PLAN.md:24-26)
  ❌ Rewrites the Database access section; one regression test with quote/backslash/Unicode IDs comes with it
B) Keep raw fragment, escape with the driver quote helper
  ✅ Smallest change to the plan text as written
  ✅ Blocks the obvious quote-break for common IDs
  ❌ Correctness depends on helper matching server charset and escape mode; hand-built SQL still needs re-audit on every edit
C) Raw fragment as written
  ✅ Zero change to the plan
  ✅ Nothing else to say for it
  ❌ Breaks the stated invariant for IDs with quotes; 500 → 72h retry loop; injection surface on the payments path
Net: one bind parameter versus owning an escape-correctness argument on the money path.

options.label: A) Bound parameter (recommended)
options.description: Parameterized query or the existing ORM finder. Regression test for quote/backslash/Unicode IDs ships with it.

options.label: B) Escape helper
options.description: Keep raw fragment, quote via DB driver helper. Charset/escape-mode dependent.

options.label: C) Raw fragment
options.description: Plan as written. Fails the opaque-TEXT invariant; injection surface.

# Plan: Payment Processing Integration — CEO Review (HOLD SCOPE)
Working plan for `/plan-ceo-review`. Source plan: `PLAN.md` on `main`.
Mode: HOLD SCOPE (explicit user choice). Review only; no code changes.
## Decision ledger

| ID and owner | Contract and evidence | Current | Proposed | Status | Exact approval and scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D2 (user) — lookup query construction | PLAN.md:16-26, 110-112; IDs opaque TEXT, unsanitized | Existing lookup (no cast/format restriction) | Raw SQL fragment from `request.params.userId` | unresolved | — |

### D2 — lookup query construction: options (pending)

Facts (PLAN.md:16-31): `request.params.userId` is an external string
forwarded unchanged; IDs are opaque TEXT with punctuation and Unicode; the
ownership guard is an identity comparison, not SQL validation. Interpolating
that string into a raw SQL fragment has two failure paths:

1. **Correctness.** A legitimate ID containing `'`, `\`, `;` or a
   multi-byte sequence breaks the fragment → DB exception → HTTP 500 →
   Stripe retries for 72h with the same string → same failure. That user's
   payment is never marked paid and the ingress alert fires every retry.
2. **Security.** Any path that lets an external party influence a stored
   user-ID binding (signup-derived IDs, imports, support tooling) turns the
   fragment into SQL injection with a valid Stripe signature attached.

| Commitment | Source/approval or pending | Current | A: Bind parameter | B: Escape/quote helper | C: Raw fragment (plan) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| No cast / no format restriction | settled, PLAN.md:24-26 | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Every nonempty string is a valid identifier | settled, PLAN.md:25-26 | yes | yes | mostly (charset-dependent) | no |
| Unknown user → 200, log, stop | settled, PLAN.md:43-44 | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Regression test: ID with quote/backslash/Unicode resolves the user | pending (D4 decides base suite; this test belongs to D2's fix) | none | yes | yes | n/a |

- **A) Bind parameter** (`WHERE id = ?` / named bind, or the ORM finder the
  existing lookup already uses). Effort S (human ~1 hr / CC ~2 min). Risk
  low. Pros: no charset edge cases; identical semantics to the existing
  lookup; injection impossible by construction. Cons: none material.
- **B) Escape via the DB driver's quote helper, keep the raw fragment.**
  Effort S. Risk medium. Pros: minimal edit to plan text. Cons: correctness
  depends on the helper matching server charset/`NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES`
  settings; still a hand-built fragment reviewers must re-audit.
- **C) Raw fragment as written.** Effort S. Risk high. Fails invariant
  PLAN.md:25-26 for IDs containing quote characters; injection surface.

Recommendation: A. Verification coverage: A gets a regression test with
IDs containing `'`, `\`, `;`, and a multi-byte string (kept with the fix
per HOLD SCOPE); B needs the same plus charset-mode tests; C has none.

Limits recorded: mail deadline 1s; DB+ingress 2s; webhook 10s; 1 new class;
planned file changes estimated 2-4 (handler, routing/flag wiring, lookup;
plus tests if D4 approves). Estimates, no code to count.
